Professional knowledge and clinical experience necessary to dispense hearing aids and provide ancillary hearing aid–related services

The Senior Audiologist provides comprehensive and specialized audiologic care within the Department of Otolaryngology. The position provides advanced diagnostic and rehabilitative services, including audiologic and vestibular assessment, hearing aid evaluation and dispensing, and bone conduction hearing device services for patients with diverse and complex hearing and balance needs.
40% - Hearing Aid Dispensing Services

As an experienced member of the clinical care team, the Senior Audiologist applies advanced clinical knowledge and judgment to evaluate patient needs, develop individualized recommendations, and provide high-quality, patient-centered care. The position also participates in the state-mandated newborn hearing program and collaborates with physicians and other healthcare professionals to support coordinated audiologic care across the patient population.
30% - Audiologic Evaluations
10% - Bone Conduction Hearing Systems
5% - Audiologic Consultation and Education
5% - Audiologic Counseling
5% - Participate In Newborn Hearing Screening Program
5% - Auditory Brainstem Response (ABR) Evaluations
Continuing professional education necessary to maintain a high level of expertise in the areas of audiology and hearing aid dispensing
Paneling by California Children's Services (CCS)
Familiarity with current hearing aids and assistive listening devices, including programmable/digital hearing aids and associated fitting software
Commitment to continuing professional education to maintain a high level of expertise in audiology and hearing aid dispensing

Ability to operate audiologic equipment including, but not limited to, two channel audiometers, middle ear analyzers, otoacoustic emissions equipment, hearing aid analyzers, ABR/ASSR equipment, and newborn hearing screening devices
Ability to assess aided hearing performance using real ear measurements, electroacoustic analysis, and functional gain measurements, as well as the knowledge to interpret results
Ability to make earmold impressions and determine appropriate earmold and custom shell designs
Knowledge and skill necessary to perform in office repairs and modifications on earmolds and hearing aids
Ability to communicate effectively with patients and their families
Ability to communicate effectively with physicians and other health care providers
Organizational skills necessary to maintain accurate records related to patient care
